_comment: HAND-COMPUTED expectations for probes/widgets/clip/Main.as. Never regenerate these by running the probe.

_derivation.layout: root: column, padding 16, gap 12, explicit [320,160]. All three boxes have an EXPLICIT [120,28]; their strips have an EXPLICIT [200,28] plus minSize [200,28] so the engine cannot shrink them into the box. Children stack in order; y = prevY + prevH + 12 starting at 16 (padding-top); x = 16 (padding-left) for all six nodes.

rects.hidden-strip: the box has no border/padding, so the child sits at the CONTENT origin = the box origin; its own width is 200 and a CLIP MUST NOT RESIZE IT -> [16,16,200,28]

points.page: (4,4) is the root's own background 0xFFFFFF (outside every box)
points.hidden-in: (131,30): local x = 131-16 = 115 < 120, so it is INSIDE the clip and under the strip -> the strip's own 0xFF0000. Proves the clip does not eat what it should show.
points.hidden-out: (145,30): local x = 129 > 120 -> 14px PAST the box, still inside the strip's 200px of layout. Clipped => the page behind (0xFFFFFF). THIS IS THE TEETH: with no clip the strip paints here (0xFF0000), which is exactly the G29 defect.
points.visible-out: (139,70): local x = 123 > 120 on the UNCLIPPED control row (y 56..84) -> the strip paints all 200px => 0x2563EB. Without this control the two points above could not distinguish 'clipped' from 'never painted'.

_derivation.program_asserts: The clip rectangle is (0,0,120,28) -- x/y 0 means PURE CLIP (a non-zero origin is scrollRect's content SHIFT, which scrollView owns) and w/h are the BORDER box (a padding-box window would shave the node's own background). 'visible' installs nothing. The clip lives on the BOX, never on the child, and the child's own scrollRect stays null (a scrollView/image inside a clipped card must keep its own crop). A re-solve that lands on the same extents REUSES the cached rectangle (extra.clipLast) instead of allocating. Hit testing follows the clip: a click 14px past the window does NOT reach the spilling strip, a click inside it does, and the same past-the-box point on the unclipped control DOES reach its strip.
